title: India's goods gap is huge. Its current account gap isn't.
sources: RBI, 'Developments in India's Balance of Payments during the First Quarter (April-June) of 2026-27', 1 September 2026

quiz.q: Which account records remittances from abroad?
quiz.why: Right. Remittances are personal transfers, recorded in the current account along with goods, services and income.

script: From April to June 2026,
From April to June twenty twenty-six,
India imported 86 billion dollars more goods than it exported.
India imported eighty-six billion dollars more goods than it exported.
Yet its current account deficit was just 4.2 billion:
Yet its current account deficit was just four point two billion:
half a percent of GDP.
half a percent of G D P.
Why? The current account also counts services and transfers.
Net services brought in 51.6 billion;
Net services brought in fifty-one point six billion;
remittance receipts, 42.9 billion.
remittance receipts, forty-two point nine billion.
The other side records investment:
textbooks call it the capital account;
RBI data calls it the financial account.
R B I data calls it the financial account.
That quarter, direct investment came in,
while portfolio money flowed out.
Goods tell half the story.
Services and remittances tell the rest.
Your turn.
Which account records remittances from abroad?

scenes.sub: Services and remittances tell the rest.

claims.claim: Q1 2026-27 (April-June 2026) merchandise trade deficit US$86.1 billion (86)
Current account deficit US$4.2 billion, 0.5% of GDP in Q1 2026-27
Net services receipts US$51.6 billion; personal transfer (remittance) receipts US$42.9 billion
Investment flows sit in the financial account in RBI's BoP data; the capital account in that format is narrow (capital transfers, non-produced non-financial assets)
Net FDI was an inflow (US$6.1 bn) and net FPI an outflow (US$9.6 bn) in Q1 2026-27

review_note: All figures from RBI's 1 September 2026 press release (primary) and are preliminary; they may be revised. The video shows 'Apr-Jun 2026' on every number. Remittance figure is gross personal transfer receipts as RBI reports it. Simplification: 'textbooks call it the capital account' reflects the older presentation; check the wording with the economy editor. Left out: reserve valuation changes, primary income, the year-ago comparison.
